annotations.title: You thought euil.
annotations.text: ◦ This plaine distinction sheweth, that sinne is wholly of the sinner; and that God hath no part therin, but turneth it to good. For those things which Iosephs brethren did against him, were occasions of his aduancement in Ægypt, through the omnipotent wisdome of God. VVhose propertie is, out of euerie euil to draw good. S. Chrisost. ho. 67. in Gen. S. Aug. Enchirid. c. 11. & li. 14. c. 27. de ciuit.

notes.text: Mans wil, not God the cause of sinne.

annotations.title: Carie my bones with you.
annotations.text: For the same reasons Ioseph would be finally buried in Chanaan, for which Iacob desired to be there buried (chap. 47.) but Ioseph would not presently be caried thither, <mn>◦</mn>lest it might haue geuen offence to the Ægyptians; or at least haue diminished their fauoure towardes his brethren: and withal he would confirme his brethren in their hope of returning, seing he was content, that his bodie should expect in Ægypt, til the whole Nation should returne into Chanaan.

notes.text: Ioseph, for his brethrés sake, differred his desired burial in Chanaan.
